title: Lineage-aware profile generation: dataset fingerprints, prompt-stitching, and runner sandboxing
creator: Elena Park
description:
Goal: Improve the benchmark harness so generated performance profiles include provable dataset lineage and reproducible prompt stitching, and run eval runners in an isolated sandbox to prevent cross-contamination. This enables reliable model onboarding and safe version pinning by producing auditable artifacts (manifest + signed fingerprints) that operators can use when promoting model versions to Dedicated/Private deployments.

Scope:
- Dataset fingerprinting: compute content-addressed checksums for dataset shards, capture provenance tags (source, ingest-time, transform-ops), and persist a manifest v2 alongside generated profiles.
- Prompt-stitching: support multi-turn prompt templates composed from multiple prompt files with deterministic seeding and instrumentation to record which prompt variant produced each sample.
- Runner sandboxing: run eval runners inside ephemeral containers/VMs or lightweight sandboxes to avoid host-state leakage (e.g., KV cache, RNG state), and capture environment metadata (kernel, CUDA/cuDNN, quantization runtime).

Why now: Onboarding failures and subtle profile drift have caused incorrect version pinning during a recent Dedicated customer rollout. Operators need stronger guarantees that a published profile maps to the exact dataset+prompts+runner environment used to generate metrics.

Out of scope: full provenance UI in Console (followup), and signed artifact distribution (separate security PR).
acceptance_criteria: Profile manifest v2 produced for every eval run containing dataset shard checksums, prompt lineage, runner image digest, and deterministic seed used
Harness has a --stitch-prompts flag that accepts a prompt manifest and emits per-sample prompt provenance in eval logs
Eval runners execute in an isolated sandbox by default and fail fast if host artifacts are mounted
End-to-end test: re-running the same manifest on a fresh worker reproduces metrics within defined tolerances (±0.5% for throughput, identical accuracy/error counts for deterministic tasks)
Documentation for onboarding engineers: how to read manifest v2, pin model+profile, and validate dataset fingerprints
Security review checklist completed and PRs approved by Security team
implementation_notes: Dataset fingerprinting: use SHA-256 over canonicalized JSON lines for text tasks and content hashing for binaries; store checksums per-shard and an aggregate manifest checksum
Prompt-stitching: implement a small DSL for prompt composition (include/merge/transform) stored as prompt-manifest.json with version field
Deterministic seeding: expose RNG seed in manifest and set both Python and runtime (TRT/cuBLAS) deterministic flags where available
Runner sandboxing: prototype with firecracker/wasm-runner for CPU-only tasks and container images for GPU runners; avoid heavy orchestration changes by leveraging existing test infra
Storage: store artifacts in s3://redwood-evals/profiles/{profile_id}/manifest-v2.json and make manifest immutably stored (write-once + object lock when supported)
Compatibility: manifest v2 must be backwards-compatible with existing consumers; include a converter tool for older profiles
qa_steps: Create a small text dataset (3 shards) and a prompt manifest with 4 stitched variants; run harness with --emit-manifest and verify checksums written
Run the same manifest twice on separate sandboxed workers and compare metrics and manifest checksums
Introduce a tiny nondeterministic operation (sleep jitter) and confirm sandboxing prevents cross-run contamination
Attempt to mount /tmp from host into sandboxed runner and assert harness rejects the run with explicit error
Run a smoke onboarding flow: upload dataset, generate profile, pin model version with the manifest; verify Console ingest (follow-up) accepts manifest metadata
